mechanically

/muh-KAN-ik-lee/ - the stress falls on KAN · adverb

Hear It

What It Means

Mechanically means automatically and without thought or feeling — going through the motions the way a machine would.

By the hundredth signing, she was smiling mechanically at each fan, her pen already moving before the book had opened.

Example

The veteran flight attendant delivered the safety briefing mechanically, hands rising and falling on cue while her eyes tracked the boarding line for empty seats.

The briefing is word-perfect — nothing is skipped — but the performance runs on rails: no attention, no feeling, gestures made the way a machine would make them. The machine hiding inside the word is literal: Greek mēchanē named a machine or engine.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

automatically: Automatically means without conscious decision, like a reflex; mechanically adds the machine's flatness — not just unbidden, but drained of feeling and attention.

robotically: Robotically means with the stiff, programmed sameness of a robot; robotically exaggerates the outward look, while mechanically points at what's missing inside — thought and feeling.

routinely: Routinely means as a regular matter of course; a task done routinely happens on schedule, but it can still be done with care — done mechanically, the care is gone.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

attentively: with full thought given to the task

thoughtfully: with real consideration and feeling

Where it sits · how much mind is left in the motion

absently → mechanically → robotically

absently vs. mechanically: Absently is milder than mechanically: an absent-minded stirrer has merely wandered off for a moment, while stirring mechanically means the mind checked out of the task long ago.

robotically vs. mechanically: Robotically pushes past mechanically: mechanically empties the motion of thought and feeling, and robotically stiffens even its look, until onlookers half expect to hear servo motors.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — mechan-: machine, engine (Greek mēchanē)

Suffix — -ical: relating to; of the nature of

Suffix — -ly: in the manner of

Put it together: Greek mēchanē named a machine or engine; -ical makes the adjective and -ly makes the adverb, so the word literally reads 'in the manner of a machine.' English put the root to work in both directions — hardware on one side, and on the other a small family of words about contrivance and how things run.

Use the root in a new word: machination: The play's second act is all machination, with three courtiers whispering behind three different curtains.

Root Check

Word Choice

flat / observational

Mechanically has a literal sense — 'by machine,' as in mechanically separated or mechanically ventilated — but the SAT's favorite is the figurative one: a person performing with the feeling switched off. Context settles which is which; a nodding witness answers mechanically, a factory bottles juice mechanically. When the emptiness needs a visible, stiff-jointed look, robotically is the stronger brush.
